parts:
This is probably the best I can do. 


asd<-structure(list(variable = structure(1:5, .Label = c("x1", "x2",

"y1", "y2", "z"), class = "factor"), value1 = c(6.23e-18, 6.43e-18, 
0.228, 0.234, 0.39), value2 = c(-0.28313269, -0.28902094, 0.01739011,

0.02151179, 0.15097369), variable2 = structure(c(1L, 1L, 2L, 
2L, 3L), .Label = c("x", "y", "z"), class = "factor"), variable3 = c(1L, 
2L, 1L, 2L, 1L)), .Names = c("variable", "value1", "value2", 
"variable2", "variable3"), class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, 
-5L))

asd2<-melt(asd[1:3])
colnames(asd2)<-c("x", "y", "z")
asd2$x<-factor(asd2$x, levels=c("z", "y2", "y1", "x2", "x1"))


ggplot(data=asd2)+
geom_bar(aes(x=x, y=z, fill=y), position="dodge")+
geom_hline(y=0, colour="red")+
geom_vline(x=0, colour="red")+
geom_vline(x=1.5, colour="blue")+
geom_vline(x=3.5, colour="green")+
geom_vline(x=5.5, colour="yellow")+
theme_bw()+
coord_flip()+
opts(panel.grid.major=theme_blank()
, panel.grid.minor=theme_blank()
, panel.background=theme_rect(colour="black"))
HTH, 

Brandon

parts: Hi Christofer,

> that?

If I understand correctly what you want, then no, you don't kneed to
know coordinates. Just do

geom_text(aes(x=x, y=z, label=round(z, digits=2)),
position=position_dodge(width=.9), size=3)

or so.

While I'm at it, here are two alternative versions. The first one
retains some of the original elements in your original example, the
second one ditches the bars and the dodging, both of which I think add
little or nothing.

asd<- structure(list(variable = structure(1:5, .Label = c("x1", "x2",
"y1", "y2", "z"), class = "factor"), value1 = c(6.23e-18, 6.43e-18,
0.228, 0.234, 0.39), value2 = c(-0.28313269, -0.28902094, 0.01739011,
0.02151179, 0.15097369)), .Names = c("variable", "value1", "value2"),
class = "data.frame", row.names = c(NA, -5L))
colnames(asd2)<-c("x", "y", "z")

asd2$x<-factor(asd2$x, levels=c("z", "y2", "y1", "x2", "x1"))

levels(asd2$x) <- c("z1", "y2", "y1", "x2", "x1")
asd3 <- cbind(colsplit(asd2[,1], split="", names=c("var", "x")), asd2[,-1])
asd3$x <- factor(asd3$x)

ggplot(data=asd3, aes(x=x, y=z, fill=y))+
geom_bar(position="dodge", stat="identity")+
geom_hline(y=0, colour="red")+
geom_point(aes(color=y), size=10, alpha=.5,
position=position_dodge(width=.9)) +
geom_point(aes(fill=NULL), color="black", size=10,
position=position_dodge(width=.9), shape=21) +
geom_text(aes(x=x, y=z, label=round(z, digits=2)),
position=position_dodge(width=.9), size=3) +
coord_flip() +
facet_grid(var ~ .) +
theme_bw()

ggplot(data=asd3, aes(x=x, y=z, fill=y))+
geom_hline(y=0, colour="red")+
geom_point(aes(color=y), size=10, alpha=.5) +
geom_point(aes(fill=NULL), color="black", size=10, shape=21) +
geom_text(aes(label=round(z, digits=2)), size=3) +
coord_flip() +
facet_grid(var ~ .) +
theme_bw()

-Ista

messages.subject: Re: How to draw this plot? Any help please?
parts:
When you map a factor you an aesthetic you can end up with multiple
geoms that occupy the same x and y coordinates. Position adjustments
are used to tell ggplot2 what to do in this situation. Example:

dat <- expand.grid(x1=c("A", "B"), x2=c("C", "D"))
dat$y <- 1:nrow(dat)

p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=x1, y=y, color=x2, fill=x2))
p + geom_bar(position="identity", alpha=.2) ## plot the bars right on
top of each other
p + geom_bar(position="stack", alpha=.2) ## stack the bars one on top
of the other
p + geom_bar(position="fill", alpha=.2) ## stack the bars one on top
of the other and standardize to equal height
ggplot(dat, aes(x=x1, y=y, color=x2, fill=x2)) +
geom_bar(position="dodge", alpha=.2) ## stack the bars one next to the
other.

## This works with different geoms, except that apparently geom_text
has no width so we have to specify manually
p + geom_text(aes(label=c("hel", "lo", "wor", "ld")), position="identity")

On Wed, Nov 10, 2010 at 11:53 PM, Ista Zahn <iz...@psych.rochester.edu> wrote:
When you map a factor you an aesthetic you can end up with multiple
geoms that occupy the same x and y coordinates. Position adjustments
are used to tell ggplot2 what to do in this situation. Example:

dat <- expand.grid(x1=c("A", "B"), x2=c("C", "D"))
dat$y <- 1:nrow(dat)

p <- ggplot(dat, aes(x=x1, y=y, color=x2, fill=x2))
p + geom_bar(position="identity", alpha=.2) ## plot the bars right on
top of each other
p + geom_bar(position="stack", alpha=.2) ## stack the bars one on top
of the other
p + geom_bar(position="fill", alpha=.2) ## stack the bars one on top
of the other and standardize to equal height
ggplot(dat, aes(x=x1, y=y, color=x2, fill=x2)) +
geom_bar(position="dodge", alpha=.2) ## stack the bars one next to the
other.

## This works with different geoms, except that apparently geom_text
has no width so we have to specify manually
p + geom_text(aes(label=c("hel", "lo", "wor", "ld")), position="identity")
p + geom_text(aes(label=c("hel", "lo", "wor", "ld")), position="stack")
p + geom_text(aes(label=c("hel", "lo", "wor", "ld")),
position="dodge") ## Doesn't do what we want (because geom_text has no
width?). So we specify the width argument to position_dodge:
p + geom_text(aes(label=c("hel", "lo", "wor", "ld")),
position=position_dodge(width=1))

-ista
